criteria.reasoning: The report profiles "Robert Frederick ("Robert F.") Smith, founder, chairman and CEO of Vista Equity Partners" and explicitly excludes the musician and the former senator: "Nothing about those people appears here." No biography, gift or legal matter of another Robert Smith is attributed to him.
The report states "Founder, Chairman and CEO of Vista Equity Partners, which he founded in 2000." Firm, current titles and founding year all match.
The report gives "B.S. in chemical engineering, Cornell University (1985); M.B.A., Columbia Business School (1994)." Discipline, schools and years are all correct.
The report states "Residence: Austin, Texas," citing the DOJ release and Forbes.
The report gives "Net worth: about $10 billion," Forbes' March 2026 figure, which is inside the $9-13 billion band.

The report identifies "Fund II Foundation, his private foundation (EIN 47-2396669)" and says "He is its founding director and President; recent 990-PFs list him as a director." It also treats the foundation as one of his giving vehicles.

The giving table gives the 2016 Cornell gift as "$30 million ($20 million to the College of Engineering plus $10 million in scholarships)." The criterion requires the $50 million total and names $30 million as a failing figure. The naming of the Smith School is correct, but the total is wrong.

The report gives the Morehouse Class of 2019 gift as "$40 million" and never mentions the final $34 million figure. The criterion fails the $40 million early estimate unless it is presented as such alongside $34 million.

The report describes SFI as an income-contingent program for STEM juniors and seniors at HBCUs, and gives "$50 million from Fund II Foundation (June 2020) plus $50 million personal gift from Smith (October 2020)." It explicitly says Cisco's $150 million and Steinbridge's $100 million are "Not his money."

The report names "Prairie View A&M University was one of SFI's first nine partner HBCUs (announced November 2020, launched fall 2021)." It also names the 2014 Huston-Tillotson commencement address and the $10,000 Fund II donation.

The report says "No major gift from Smith to a Texas HBCU is on record. Fund II Foundation's only Texas HBCU grant is a $10,000 donation to Prairie View A&M in 2021." It invents no other gift and no named fund at a Texas HBCU.

The report dates the NPA correctly (October 15, 2020) and describes the offshore scheme, but gives the payment as "agreed to pay $182 million in taxes and penalties." The criterion names $182 million as a failing figure, since that is the refund claims he abandoned, not the more than $139 million he paid.
The report states "He was not charged. He admitted the conduct, agreed to cooperate." It does not mention an indictment or conviction, does not mention Brockman, and does not say he was cleared.

The report recommends raising the matter with Smith: "In the first meeting, acknowledge his cooperation with the Justice Department as a story of accountability and second chances that fits the program's values." The criterion names praising his cooperation with prosecutors in conversation as a failing example.
The report gives capacity as "$25-50 million" and the ask as "$10 million over five years." Both are dollar figures, and the ask does not exceed the capacity.

The report contradicts the fact sheet in three graded places. It gives the 2016 Cornell total as $30 million (sheet: $50 million), the Morehouse Class of 2019 gift as $40 million (sheet: $34 million; $40 million was an early estimate), and the NPA payment as $182 million in taxes and penalties (sheet: more than $139 million, with $182 million being the abandoned refund claims).
